communities.report: This community links three distinct geographic/historical clusters within the United States. In West Virginia, Justice, West Virginia is a census-designated place in Mingo County (which is itself a county in West Virginia), located along U.S. Route 52, southeast of the town of Gilbert; Justice had a population of 412 as recorded by the 2010 census, and it has a post office with ZIP code 24851. In California, Stinson Beach, California is a census-designated place in Marin County, California, situated on the west coast of the United States, located east-southeast of Bolinas; the 2010 census recorded Stinson Beach's population as 632. Separately, the KVLY-TV mast, a guyed mast built in 1963 standing 628.8 m (2,063 ft) tall and used for VHF-UHF transmission, is the tallest mast in the world and is located in Blanchard, North Dakota, itself a location within the United States. The community also covers early American frontier history: after the Revolution, the British ceded lands between the Appalachian Mountains and the Mississippi River to the United States via the Treaty of Paris, lands then inhabited by tribes including the Shawnee, Cherokee, and Choctaw, all of whom were compelled to sign away territory in postwar treaties with the United States. Disputes over this land settlement provoked war in the Northwest Territory; the United States suffered its most severe defeat at the hands of American Indians at the Battle of the Wabash in 1791 during this conflict. In response, President Washington dispatched a newly trained army to the Northwest Territory, which went on to decisively defeat the Indian confederacy—a coalition of American Indian tribes—at the Battle of Fallen Timbers in 1794.

This community centers on Canadian cultural and business entities linked through geography and industry connections in Ontario, Canada. Three Gut Records, an independent record label founded in 1999, was based in Guelph, Ontario, Canada, and was co-founded by Lisa Moran and Tyler Clarke Burke; its releases were distributed by Outside Music, and the label achieved a breakout success with the Canadian band Constantines, whose self-titled 2001 album was released on Three Gut Records. Guelph, Ontario is located within Canada, as is the broader province of Ontario, which contains the city of Toronto. Toronto serves as the headquarters location for Marketwired, a press release distribution service founded in 1993 and incorporated in the United States in 1999; Marketwired distributes press releases via two traditional methods/services, Associated Press and Bloomberg. Toronto is also significant as the setting, during the early 1980s, for the 1983 Canadian science fiction body horror film Videodrome, which was written and directed by David Cronenberg and starred James Woods, Deborah Harry, and Sonja Smits.

This community centers on the animated television series American Dad!, an American animated television series, and its fictional character Steve Smith (full name Steven Anita "Steve" Smith), who is voiced by actor Scott Grimes. Steve Smith is the only son of both Stan Smith (his father) and Francine Smith (his mother), and he is the younger brother of Hayley, his older sister. American Dad! also includes the episode "Rapture's Delight," the ninth episode of the sixth season, which originally aired on December 13, 2009, on the Fox television network. In this episode, Steve is raptured along with his sister Hayley. The episode's main characters are Francine and Stan, whose marriage and relationship come to an end after mutual blame arises over the rapture event. During the episode, Francine befriends a man who is later revealed to be Jesus, and she subsequently becomes his bride. Separately, the character Stan (distinct in context but connected via character identity) is portrayed by French performer Arnaud Joyet, a singer, musician, comedian, and theatre director born on 3 April 1974, who plays Stan in the series Hero Corp, in which Stan is a character.

This community centers on Trey Parker, the voice actor for the animated series South Park, who provides the voice for numerous main and recurring characters. Among the main characters he voices are Eric Cartman, Mr. Garrison, Randy Marsh, and Stan Marsh. Among the recurring characters he voices are Clyde Donovan, Jimmy Valmer, Mr. Hankey, Mr. Mackey, Phillip, Stephen Stotch, Timmy Burch, and Tuong Lu Kim. Each of these characters—Clyde Donovan, Eric Cartman, Jimmy Valmer, Mr. Garrison, Mr. Hankey, Mr. Mackey, Phillip, Randy Marsh, Stan Marsh, Stephen Stotch, Timmy Burch, and Tuong Lu Kim—is directly linked to Trey Parker through a "voices" relation, reflecting his role as their voice actor within the South Park franchise. The relation is bidirectional in naming convention for Tuong Lu Kim, explicitly noted as Trey Parker voicing Tuong Lu Kim, while the other characters are listed as voicing (being voiced by) Trey Parker, underscoring his extensive and central role as the primary voice performer for a wide range of the show's cast, spanning both its principal figures and its supporting, recurring cast members.

This community centers on Irish actor Aidan Turner (born 19 June 1983), whose career is defined by a series of notable television and film roles. Turner played Kíli in the three-part fantasy film The Hobbit, and portrayed Ruairí McGowan in the television series The Clinic. He also played John Mitchell, the central character of the supernatural drama television series Being Human. In Desperate Romantics, Turner took on the role of Dante Gabriel Rossetti. His most prominent role is Ross Poldark, the titular character from The Poldark Novels, a novel series written by author Winston Graham. This literary work was adapted by the BBC (British Broadcasting Corporation) in 2015 into a television series, in which Turner starred as Ross Poldark, bringing together the community's key figures: Aidan Turner as the connecting actor, the BBC as the adapting production organization, Winston Graham as the original author, and the interconnected web of characters—Kíli, Ruairí McGowan, John Mitchell, Dante Gabriel Rossetti, and Ross Poldark—that define Turner's acting career across The Hobbit, The Clinic, Being Human, Desperate Romantics, and the 2015 Poldark adaptation.

This community centers on the 1989 film UHF, co-written by musician-comedian Yankovic and his collaborator Levey, who together applied parody and comedy techniques to the screenplay. The film features the character George, portrayed as a straight man with a vivid imagination. Principal filming of UHF took place in and around Tulsa, Oklahoma, with many of the extras drawn from Dallas, Texas, indicating that both Tulsa and the Dallas area contributed personnel to the production. The film received crucial financing support from Orion Pictures, a studio co-founded in 1978, after cost assurances were secured. Orion Pictures itself is linked to Mike Medavoy (full name Morris Mike Medavoy, born January 21, 1941), an American film producer and executive who co-founded the studio in 1978. Medavoy's career spans several major studios: he served as head of production at United Artists from 1974 to 1978, was later former chairman of TriStar Pictures, and currently serves as chairman and CEO of Phoenix Pictures. Thus, the community links UHF's creative team (Yankovic, Levey, and the character George) and its production geography (Tulsa and Dallas) to the broader industry network surrounding Orion Pictures and Mike Medavoy's extensive executive history across United Artists, TriStar Pictures, and Phoenix Pictures.

The Linden Hills Library is a public library located in the Linden Hills neighborhood of southwest Minneapolis, Minnesota (a city situated in the state of Minnesota), and it opened in 1911 on the first floor of the Lake Harriet Commercial Club building. In 1931, under the leadership of Gratia Countryman—who served as chief librarian of the Minneapolis Public Library, the system that oversaw the branch's move—the library relocated into its own building at 2900 West 43rd Street. That building was designed in the Tudor Revival style by Joseph Victor Vanderbilt, an area resident. Edith Frost served as the library's head librarian for over thirty years. In recognition of its historical and architectural significance, the Linden Hills Library was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2000, and it was later renovated in 2002.

Kirtland Records is a record label founded in 2003 by John Kirtland and his wife Jenny Kirtland, who also serves as a choir member of The Polyphonic Spree, one of the Texas-based indie bands signed to the label. Kirtland Records serves as the record label for a roster of Texas-based indie acts, including The Polyphonic Spree, Toadies, The Vanished, Burden Brothers, and Sarah Jaffe. The label secured a national distribution deal with RED Distribution, a deal made possible by leveraging the back catalog rights of the band Bush. Through this arrangement, Kirtland Records gained wider distribution access via RED Distribution while continuing to serve as the home label for its Texas-based indie artists.

This community centers on WCCO-TV, a CBS owned-and-operated television station broadcasting on virtual channel 4 (UHF digital channel 32), which serves the Twin Cities television market. WCCO-TV is owned by CBS Television Stations, a subsidiary of CBS Corporation, establishing a clear corporate ownership chain from CBS Corporation down through CBS Television Stations to WCCO-TV itself. The station is licensed to Minneapolis, Minnesota, and its studios are physically located on South 11th Street, a street situated in downtown Minneapolis that runs along Nicollet Mall. Separately, WCCO-TV's transmitter is located at the Telefarm complex, which is situated in Shoreview, Minnesota. Together, these relations map out both the corporate ownership structure behind WCCO-TV and the geographic footprint of its operations, spanning studio facilities in downtown Minneapolis and transmission infrastructure in Shoreview, Minnesota, all in service of the broader Twin Cities television market.

communities.report: This community centers on the legal concept of territorial waters (also called the territorial sea), defined as the belt of coastal waters extending at most 12 nautical miles (equivalent to 22.2 km or 13.8 mi) from the baseline of a coastal state. This maximum extent and the definition of territorial waters are established by the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, an international treaty from 1982. The baseline used to measure territorial waters is usually the mean low-water mark of a coastal state, and this baseline belongs to that coastal state. Territorial waters are regarded as the sovereign territory of the coastal state from which they are measured, and this sovereignty extends beyond the waters themselves to include the airspace above the territorial sea and the seabed below it. Despite this sovereignty, territorial waters allow certain rights of passage for foreign vessels: innocent passage permits foreign civilian ships to pass through, while transit passage specifically applies to passage through straits within territorial waters. Additionally, territorial waters are subject to maritime delimitation, the term in international law for the process of adjusting territorial sea boundaries between states.

This community centers on GeminiJets, a diecast model airplane manufacturer based in Las Vegas, Nevada, United States, which is located in the state of Nevada. GeminiJets was founded in 1998 under the original name SkyJets before adopting its current name. The company's product line was established by its founding company, ADI (Airliners Distributing Inc.), which serves as the organizational backbone behind GeminiJets. ADI holds production licenses obtained from four major aircraft manufacturers—Airbus, Boeing, McDonnell Douglas, and Embraer—allowing it to produce licensed diecast models based on aircraft designs from these companies. This network of relationships establishes GeminiJets' operational foundation: its geographic base in Las Vegas, Nevada; its origin story as SkyJets in 1998; and its licensing relationships, mediated through ADI, with Airbus, Boeing, McDonnell Douglas, and Embraer, which collectively enable the manufacture of its diecast model airplane products.

This community centers on Gamla stan metro station, a station of the Stockholm metro located in the Gamla stan district of Stockholm, which opened on 24 November 1957. The station is served by two lines: the Green line and the Red line. The Green line was formed by a 1957 connection linking the east and west parts of the network via Slussen and Hötorget, with the Green line connecting to both Slussen and Hötorget. The Red line's first stretch opened on 5 April 1964, running between T-Centralen, where it started, and Fruängen, where it ended. Together, these relations show Gamla stan metro station as a key interchange point within the broader Stockholm metro system, linking major locations including Slussen, Hötorget, T-Centralen, and Fruängen through its two serving lines.

John Bell is a Scottish actor born October 20, 1997, whose career spans both film and television roles. He portrayed Angus in the film Battleship, and separately took on the role of Helius in Wrath of the Titans. On television, John Bell played the character Toby Coleman in the series Tracy Beaker Returns. He also had a significant recurring role as Bain in the Hobbit film series, appearing as this character in two separate installments of the franchise. Across these varied projects, John Bell has consistently portrayed distinct characters—Angus, Bain, Helius, and Toby Coleman—demonstrating range across the film and television mediums represented by Battleship, Wrath of the Titans, the Hobbit film series, and Tracy Beaker Returns.

This community centers on Manu Bennett (full name Jonathan Manu Bennett, born 10 October 1969), a New Zealand-Australian actor known for portraying several notable characters across television and film. Manu Bennett acted in Arrow, where he portrayed the character Slade Wilson / Deathstroke. He also acted in Spartacus, playing the character Crixus. In The Shannara Chronicles, Manu Bennett acted in the series and portrayed the character Allanon. Additionally, he acted in the Hobbit film trilogy, in which he portrayed the character Azog the Defiler. Each character is directly tied to its respective production: Slade Wilson / Deathstroke is a character in Arrow; Crixus is a character in Spartacus; Allanon is a character in The Shannara Chronicles; and Azog the Defiler is a character in the Hobbit film trilogy. Together, these relations illustrate Manu Bennett's range as an actor, having portrayed four distinct characters—Allanon, Azog the Defiler, Crixus, and Slade Wilson / Deathstroke—across four major productions: The Shannara Chronicles, the Hobbit film trilogy, Spartacus, and Arrow.

This community centers on the fictional character Buzz Lightyear, a spin-off figure who has been featured across multiple media formats: the Toy Story film series, a standalone Buzz Lightyear movie, a TV series, video games, and Disney Parks attractions. The character has been voiced by three distinct performers, each associated with specific media: Tim Allen voiced Buzz Lightyear in both the Toy Story film series and the standalone Buzz Lightyear movie; Patrick Warburton provided the character's voice for the TV series; and Pat Fraley voiced Buzz Lightyear for video games as well as for the Disney Parks attractions featuring the character. These relationships establish a clear division of voice work by medium—Tim Allen for theatrical/film appearances (Toy Story and the Buzz Lightyear movie), Patrick Warburton for television, and Pat Fraley for both video games and theme park attractions—illustrating how a single character has been adapted and voiced differently depending on the platform.

This community centers on the death, burial, and commemoration of Dwight D. Eisenhower, the American president, who was buried as a General of the Army following his death. His body was transported by funeral train to Abilene, Kansas, the town where he was ultimately interred. There, Eisenhower was laid to rest in a chapel located on the grounds of the Eisenhower Presidential Library. At his burial, his body wore several military honors: the Army Distinguished Service Medal, adorned with three oak leaf clusters, as well as the Navy Distinguished Service Medal and the Legion of Merit. Eisenhower was buried alongside his son, Doud, who had died at the young age of 3 in 1921. Later, his wife, Mamie, was buried next to him after her own death in 1979, reuniting the family within the same burial site at Abilene, Kansas.

SICRAL 1B is a military communications satellite and dual-use spacecraft built by Thales Alenia Space for the Italian Armed Forces, designed to be operable for 13 years, and based on the Italsat 3000 satellite bus. Once operational, its transmission capacity will be shared among multiple users: the Italian defense ministry, NATO, and Telespazio, all of whom will draw on the satellite's communications resources for their respective needs, reflecting SICRAL 1B's role as a multi-purpose asset serving both national defense and allied military communication requirements, as well as commercial or governmental telecommunications interests through Telespazio.

Salix arbuscula, commonly known as the mountain willow, is a low, much-branched shrub that grows to a height of 0.7 metres. It has a limited distribution within Northern Europe, occurring specifically from north Scandinavia eastwards, with its range extending as far as Siberia to the east. Within Scotland, the species is characteristically found on damp rocky mountain slopes and ledges, but its Scottish occurrence is highly restricted, being rarely found outside of the areas of Perthshire and Argyll.

Sleaszy Rider Records is an independent record label founded in 1999 by Tolis G. Palantzas, with its head office located in Greece. The label operates as a distribution hub within Greece, handling the local distribution of releases from several international labels, including Pagan Records, Roadrunner Records, and SPV, all of which rely on Sleaszy Rider Records to bring their music to the Greek market. Beyond its distribution role for these partner labels domestically, Sleaszy Rider Records itself is primarily distributed across the wider European market by Sony Music/EMI, establishing a network in which the Greek-based label serves as both a recipient of distribution services from major European entities and a provider of distribution services for other labels within its home country of Greece.

This community centers on the common nightingale, a migratory insectivorous bird species that breeds across Europe and south-west Asia in forest and scrub habitats, and winters in sub-Saharan Africa, completing an extensive annual migratory cycle between these regions. The common nightingale is notably absent from the Americas, a continent where it is not naturally found. It is closely related to the thrush nightingale (Luscinia luscinia), a species that shares habitat characteristics but occupies a more northerly distribution, while the common nightingale itself maintains a more southerly range by comparison. Research into the common nightingale's favoured breeding habitat has been conducted in Germany, contributing to the scientific understanding of its ecological preferences within its broader European and south-west Asian breeding range.

Amblin Entertainment is an American film production company founded in 1981 by director and producer Steven Spielberg, alongside co-founders and film producers Kathleen Kennedy and Frank Marshall. The company's headquarters are located on the backlot of Universal Studios, which is itself situated in Universal City, California. Amblin Entertainment maintains a close relationship with Amblin Partners, distributing all films produced by Amblin Partners under the Amblin Entertainment name. This structure reflects the collaborative founding partnership between Spielberg, Kennedy, and Marshall, who established the company in 1981, and its enduring physical presence at the Universal Studios lot in Universal City, California.

Falling Waters, West Virginia is a census-designated place (CDP) located in Berkeley County, West Virginia, situated on the Potomac River. It lies along Williamsport Pike (US 11), positioned north of the nearby town of Martinsburg. According to the 2010 census, Falling Waters had a population of 876. The community holds a notable historical claim: in 1887, the publication Scientific American published an article asserting that the first U.S. railroad was built in Falling Waters in 1814, attributing this significant early railroad construction to the location.

members: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
communities.report: The Clerke Rocks are a group of small rocky islands situated southeast of South Georgia, forming a chain that extends from east to west. This island group is administratively part of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, a British Overseas Territory. At the northeastern end of the Clerke Rocks group lie The Office Boys, while at the southeastern end is Nobby, a rock also known by its Spanish-language names, Islote Llamativo or Roca Notable. Despite the British administration of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, Argentina claims sovereignty over the Clerke Rocks, asserting that they form part of Tierra del Fuego Province, an Argentine province, thereby placing the Clerke Rocks at the center of an overlapping territorial claim between the two nations.

This community centers on **Le Mauricien**, a French-language newspaper founded in 1908 that is based and distributed in **Mauritius**; it is released daily and stands as one of the most widely read newspapers in the country, notable also for its status as an independent newspaper. Le Mauricien is published by **Le Mauricien Ltd.**, the organization responsible for its production and distribution. Beyond Le Mauricien itself, Le Mauricien Ltd. serves as a broader publishing entity, also producing three additional publications: **Turf Magazine**, **Week-End**, and **Week-End Scope**. Together, these relations illustrate a media network in Mauritius anchored by a century-old, independent, daily French-language newspaper, supported by a publishing company with a diversified portfolio spanning news (Le Mauricien), weekend-oriented content (Week-End and Week-End Scope), and specialized interest material (Turf Magazine).

"The Hobbit (South Park)" is the tenth and final episode of the seventeenth season of the animated television series South Park, standing as the 247th episode overall in the show's run. It premiered on Comedy Central, the American television network responsible for airing South Park, on December 11, 2013. The episode's plot centers on two intertwined storylines: Wendy Testaburger's attempts to raise awareness of the media's impact on body image, and rapper Kanye West's crusade to convince the world that his fiancée, Kim Kardashian, is not a hobbit, despite accusations within the episode's plot suggesting otherwise. Kanye West, as Kim Kardashian's fiancé, is depicted defending her against these hobbit accusations throughout the episode, making his relationship to her and his mission a central comedic thread of this particular South Park installment.

This community centers on filmmaker Kevin Smith and his 2011 venture into independent film distribution. At the 2011 Sundance Film Festival, Kevin Smith made a notable announcement regarding the release plans for his movie Red State, revealing his intention to bypass traditional distribution methods in favor of a self-organized touring release. Following this announcement, Kevin Smith founded SModcast Pictures in 2011, establishing it as an American film distribution company as well as a film and television production company. Red State, directed and created by Kevin Smith, became the flagship release for this new venture, with SModcast Pictures serving as the distribution company used to bring the film to audiences through touring rather than conventional theatrical distribution channels. This interconnected set of events illustrates Kevin Smith's direct control over the entire lifecycle of Red State—from its creation and public announcement at a major industry festival, to the founding of his own company specifically to handle its distribution, to the unconventional touring release strategy that defined how the film ultimately reached viewers.

Equity Music Group was an American country music record label founded in 2003 by singer Clint Black. The label was distributed by Koch Entertainment, a company that has since undergone a name change and is now known as E1 Entertainment. This community centers on the relationships between Clint Black as the founder of Equity Music Group, and the corporate distribution and rebranding history connecting Koch Entertainment to its current identity as E1 Entertainment, which handled the distribution of Equity Music Group's releases within the country music industry.

This community centers on the building located at 1222 Fourth Street Southeast, which originally served as the State Capitol Credit Union building. The building was designed by master architect Ralph Rapson, who created the structure that would later become the Southeast Library. On December 29, 1966, the State Capitol Credit Union building was purchased with the intent of converting it into a library, and this conversion process culminated in the opening of the Southeast Library in 1967. Thus, the Southeast Library occupies the same physical structure at 1222 Fourth Street Southeast that Ralph Rapson designed, with its origins as a credit union building purchased and repurposed through this transformation.

Dog Star Man is a series of short experimental films released between 1961 and 1964, comprising a prelude and four parts. The entire series was directed by Stan Brakhage, who created all the films within it. The series prominently features Jane Wodening as a performer, marking her as a key figure in this body of experimental cinematic work. Together, these elements form a tightly interconnected community centered on Brakhage's directorial vision and Wodening's on-screen presence across the multi-part film project spanning the early 1960s.

This community centers on the Secchi disk, a plain white circular disk created in 1865, and its creator, Angelo Secchi, an Italian person credited with inventing this device that same year, 1865. The Secchi disk serves as a practical instrument used to measure water transparency or turbidity, functioning as the tool from which the Secchi depth is determined—the specific measure of depth at which the disk is no longer visible when lowered into a body of water, directly correlating with the level of water turbidity present. The relational structure of this community is straightforward yet foundational: Angelo Secchi created the Secchi disk in 1865, establishing his role as the originator of this scientific measurement tool, while the Secchi depth as a concept relies entirely on the Secchi disk for its practical application, being derived from observations made using this device to assess and quantify water clarity. Together, these three entities—the person Angelo Secchi, the physical instrument known as the Secchi disk, and the resulting measurement metric called Secchi depth—form an interconnected system for scientific water quality assessment that originated in 1865 and continues to link the inventor's name to both the tool and the depth measurement standard it produces.

The Appalachian Mountains, a major mountain range in eastern North America, hold particular significance as the geographic marker delineating the eastern boundary of ceded lands in this context. Functioning as a natural and political demarcation line, the Appalachian Mountains served to define the extent of territory that was surrendered or transferred, establishing the range itself as the easternmost limit of these ceded lands. As the sole community member in this dataset, the Appalachian Mountains stand as the key spatial reference point, with no other entities or relations currently documented in connection with this geographic feature beyond its defining role as a boundary marker for the ceded territory.

The Mississippi River, a place entity within this community, is defined specifically by its function as a boundary marker in territorial cession—serving as the western boundary of ceded lands. This positions the river not merely as a geographic feature but as a legally and politically significant demarcation line, delineating the extent of a land cession agreement (the specific parties, treaty, or date of cession are not detailed in the available data, but the relation explicitly identifies the Mississippi River as marking where the ceded territory ends on its western edge). No further attributes, dates, or additional relations are provided for this entity within the current community structure; the sole documented fact is this boundary-defining role, which situates the Mississippi River as a key reference point for understanding the geographic scope of the associated land cession.
